papers.title: TGR-EvoDAG: A DAG-based Multi-Agent Code Evolution Framework for Generative Recommendation on Tencent
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have enabled automated code evolution for algorithm discovery. However, current recursive self-improvement (RSI) research for sequential recommendation faces a dilemma: general-purpose frameworks lack domain-specific feedback, while recommender-specific frameworks rely on linear evolution. Crucially, naively integrating them fails when applied to Generative Recommendation (GR). Unlike end-to-end models, GR relies on a module-cascaded pipeline (tokenization, pre-training, and alignment). In this paradigm, existing evolution methods suffer from: i) cost blindness, squandering budgets by ignoring stage-asymmetric retraining overheads; and ii) short-sighted evaluation, discarding promising upstream innovations that temporarily regress metrics before downstream adaptation. To bridge these gaps, we propose TGR-EvoDAG, a multi-agent code evolution framework tailored for GR. TGR-EvoDAG models code evolution as a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) to maintain multiple evolution branches and merge complementary innovations, unifying advanced search with rich GR diagnostic feedback. We further introduce stage-aware cost planning to optimize GPU-hour budgets, and active downstream co-adaptation to navigate temporary regressions and unlock cross-stage gains. On public Amazon datasets, TGR-EvoDAG enables the first autonomous evolution of a complete GR pipeline, improving offline metrics by up to 37.4% and Agent4Rec simulated user satisfaction by 19.7% over the strongest baseline. Furthermore, in industrial deployment on Tencent's large-scale commercial media platform, the evolved GR achieves a 12.16% relative improvement in offline Hit@1 and a statistically significant 0.40% increase in online click-through rate (CTR).
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）智能体已使算法发现的自动化代码演化成为可能。然而，当前面向序列推荐的递归自我改进（RSI）研究面临两难：通用框架缺乏领域特定反馈，而推荐专用框架依赖线性演化。关键在于，将二者简单结合并应用于生成式推荐（GR）时会失败。与端到端模型不同，GR 依赖模块级联流水线（分词、预训练和对齐）。在这一范式中，现有演化方法存在以下问题：i）成本盲视，因忽略各阶段不对称的再训练开销而浪费预算；ii）评估短视，丢弃那些在下游适配前暂时使指标回退、但具有前景的上游创新。为弥补这些差距，我们提出 TGR-EvoDAG，一个为 GR 量身定制的多智能体代码演化框架。TGR-EvoDAG 将代码演化建模为有向无环图（DAG），以维护多条演化分支并合并互补创新，将先进搜索与丰富的 GR 诊断反馈统一起来。我们进一步引入阶段感知成本规划以优化 GPU 小时预算，并引入主动下游协同适配以应对暂时回退并释放跨阶段收益。在公开 Amazon 数据集上，TGR-EvoDAG 首次实现了完整 GR 流水线的自主演化，相较最强基线将离线指标提升最多 37.4%，并将 Agent4Rec 模拟用户满意度提升 19.7%。此外，在腾讯大规模商业媒体平台的工业部署中，演化后的 GR 在离线 Hit@1 上取得 12.16% 的相对提升，在线点击率（CTR）取得统计显著的 0.40% 提升。
papers.tldr_zh: TGR-EvoDAG 将生成式推荐的代码演化建模为有向无环图，结合阶段感知成本规划与下游协同适配，在 Amazon 数据集和腾讯工业部署中提升离线与在线指标。

papers.title: Accordion: Elastic-Depth Inference via Fixed-Prefix Layer Looping
papers.abstract_en: Large language models serve applications with diverse inference budgets, but training and maintaining separate models for each budget incurs substantial costs. Recent Looped Transformers enable flexible inference computation through parameter reuse, but maintaining strong performance across different inference budgets remains an open challenge. We introduce Accordion, a mixture-of-experts-based model that supports five inference budgets through fixed-prefix layer looping. Each budget follows a pre-defined execution path, while the minimum budget retains the unlooped model. Joint pretraining samples one budget per micro-batch and optimizes its next-token prediction loss without additional cross-budget consistency objectives. We further preserve these inference budgets through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, where parameter-group merging and budget-matched multi-teacher on-policy distillation integrate three domain experts into one model. After 3.6T tokens of pretraining, increasing inference depth improves Accordion-6B-A0.5B's five-category macro-average across 37 tasks by 3.01 percentage points, with the middle budget capturing 89% of this gain using half as many additional layer executions. The final model surpasses each domain expert on its corresponding task-and-budget average, while achieving strong instruction-following performance across all budgets and retaining depth-dependent gains in mathematical reasoning and code generation.
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型服务于推理预算各异的多种应用，但为每种预算训练和维护单独模型会带来巨大成本。近期的循环 Transformer 通过参数复用实现灵活的推理计算，但在不同推理预算下保持强劲性能仍是一个未解难题。我们提出 Accordion，一种基于混合专家、通过固定前缀层循环支持五种推理预算的模型。每种预算遵循预定义的执行路径，而最小预算保留未循环的模型。联合预训练在每个微批次采样一种预算并优化其下一词预测损失，不设额外的跨预算一致性目标。我们进一步通过监督微调和强化学习保留这些推理预算，其中参数组合并与预算匹配的多教师在线策略蒸馏将三个领域专家整合为一个模型。经过 3.6T token 的预训练后，增加推理深度使 Accordion-6B-A0.5B 在 37 个任务上的五类宏平均提升 3.01 个百分点，中间预算以一半的额外层执行次数获得该增益的 89%。最终模型在各自对应的任务与预算平均上超过每个领域专家，同时在所有预算下实现强劲的指令遵循性能，并在数学推理和代码生成中保持随深度变化的增益。
papers.tldr_zh: Accordion 通过固定前缀层循环与混合专家结构支持五种推理预算，经联合预训练及监督微调、强化学习保留各预算，在 37 个任务上随推理深度增加而提升。

papers.title: CASE: Confusion-Aware Skill Evolution for Frozen Multimodal Emotion Models
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially advanced Multimodal Emotion Recognition (MER) by enabling fine-grained emotion understanding through reasoning over multimodal evidence. However, they still exhibit systematic confusion between semantically adjacent emotions with highly overlapping multimodal cues. Existing approaches typically address these errors through global parameter adaptation, making confusion correction costly and inflexible. We instead observe that emotion confusion is highly localized and therefore better addressed through reusable pair-specific expertise. Building on this insight, we propose Confusion-Aware Skill Evolution (CASE), the first agent-skill framework for MER. CASE maintains a sparse, self-evolving library of pair-specific EmotionSkills that externalize affective expertise from model parameters, enabling the learned expertise to be continuously refined and readily transferred across diverse frozen MLLM backbones. During inference, CASE dynamically retrieves the appropriate EmotionSkill to reinforce boundary-aware reasoning while keeping the MLLM backbone frozen. Extensive experiments on CA-MER, DFEW, and EMER demonstrate the effectiveness and transferability of CASE across both general-purpose and emotion-specialized MLLMs. Notably, CASE improves the average accuracy of Qwen3-VL-8B on the CA-MER benchmark from 46.80% to 59.13%, while achieving consistent gains across MLLMs.
papers.abstract_zh: 多模态大语言模型（MLLM）通过对多模态证据进行推理实现细粒度情感理解，显著推进了多模态情感识别（MER）。然而，它们仍在语义相邻、多模态线索高度重叠的情感之间表现出系统性混淆。现有方法通常通过全局参数适配来处理这些错误，使混淆纠正代价高昂且不灵活。我们转而观察到情感混淆高度局部化，因此更适合通过可复用的成对特定专长来处理。基于这一洞见，我们提出混淆感知技能演化（CASE），这是首个面向 MER 的智能体技能框架。CASE 维护一个稀疏、自演化的成对特定 EmotionSkills 库，将情感专长从模型参数中外化，使学到的专长能够持续精炼并易于迁移到多种冻结的 MLLM 骨干上。推理时，CASE 动态检索合适的 EmotionSkill 以强化边界感知推理，同时保持 MLLM 骨干冻结。在 CA-MER、DFEW 和 EMER 上的大量实验证明了 CASE 在通用和情感专用 MLLM 上的有效性与可迁移性。值得注意的是，CASE 将 Qwen3-VL-8B 在 CA-MER 基准上的平均准确率从 46.80% 提升至 59.13%，并在各 MLLM 上取得一致增益。
papers.tldr_zh: CASE 以稀疏自演化的成对情感技能库外化专长，在冻结 MLLM 骨干下动态检索技能强化边界推理，将 Qwen3-VL-8B 在 CA-MER 上从 46.80% 提升至 59.13%。

匹配 MLLM / VLM：multimodal large language model

papers.title: Video-MemComp: Taylor-Guided Sensitivity-Aware Memory Management for Streaming Video Understanding
papers.abstract_en: The rapid growth of video data has created an urgent need for efficient video understanding systems that can handle long and continuous visual inputs, posing significant challenges for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) due to severe memory bottlenecks. Moreover, existing compression methods often overlook the explosive accumulation of approximation errors. To address this issue, we propose Video-MemComp, a training-free and sensitivity-aware context management framework for memory-constrained streaming video understanding. Our method theoretically decomposes compression error into orthogonal local approximation error and layer-wise structural sensitivity via a first-order Taylor expansion. To minimize local approximation error, we perform token aggregation in a pre-RoPE safe zone with an attention-conserving logit bias, mitigating geometric distortions caused by RoPE rotations. To manage layer-wise structural sensitivity, we dynamically allocate the KV cache budget based on offline gradient priors and online context entropy, prioritizing high-sensitivity layers. Video-MemComp outperforms or achieves performance comparable to full-cache and state-of-the-art compression methods on benchmarks including MLVU, VideoMME, and EgoSchema. Notably, it improves the overall accuracy of Qwen2.5-VL-3B from 62.3% to 64.1% while reducing the KV cache to an equivalent of 6,000 tokens per layer, saving over 90% of KV memory.
papers.abstract_zh: 视频数据的快速增长迫切需要能够处理长时连续视觉输入的高效视频理解系统，而严重的内存瓶颈给多模态大语言模型（MLLM）带来重大挑战。此外，现有压缩方法往往忽视近似误差的爆炸式累积。为解决这一问题，我们提出 Video-MemComp，一个面向内存受限流式视频理解的无训练、敏感度感知上下文管理框架。我们的方法通过一阶泰勒展开从理论上将压缩误差分解为正交的局部近似误差与逐层结构敏感度。为最小化局部近似误差，我们在 RoPE 之前的安全区内进行 token 聚合，并采用注意力保持的 logit 偏置，缓解 RoPE 旋转引起的几何失真。为管理逐层结构敏感度，我们基于离线梯度先验和在线上下文熵动态分配 KV 缓存预算，优先考虑高敏感度层。Video-MemComp 在 MLVU、VideoMME 和 EgoSchema 等基准上优于或达到与全缓存及最先进压缩方法相当的性能。值得注意的是，它将 Qwen2.5-VL-3B 的整体准确率从 62.3% 提升至 64.1%，同时将 KV 缓存降至每层等效 6,000 token，节省超过 90% 的 KV 内存。
papers.tldr_zh: Video-MemComp 用一阶泰勒展开将压缩误差分解为局部近似误差与逐层敏感度，在 RoPE 前安全区聚合 token 并按敏感度分配 KV 预算，节省超 90% KV 内存且提升准确率。

papers.title: PCFBench: How Far Can Large Vision-Language Models Go in Physics-aware Photonic Inverse Design?
papers.abstract_en: Photonic crystal fibers (PCFs) underpin critical applications in telecommunications, sensing, and high-power laser delivery, yet their design remains a manual, expert-intensive process that couples geometric intuition with deep waveguide physics. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising path toward automating PCF design, but can they truly reason about photonic physics from microscopy images, or do they merely recognize visual patterns? We introduce PCFBench, the first comprehensive benchmark for evaluating VLMs on the perception, reasoning, and decision steps of the photonic inverse-design loop. PCFBench spans 26 tasks organized into six categories of increasing cognitive demand (Geometry Perception, Physics Understanding, Text Generation, Multi-modal Reasoning, Inverse-Design Decision, and Code Generation), built from over 220K FDTD simulation samples across 18 structurally diverse fiber families. We evaluate both individual VLMs on isolated tasks and multi-agent systems (MAS) on the full sequential pipeline from perception to design. Our results reveal a striking perception-design gap: current models can identify fiber geometry with moderate success, yet consistently fail to translate that visual understanding into physics-aware design actions. Moreover, cascading agents through the pipeline exposes significant error propagation, where upstream perception mistakes compound into downstream design failures. These findings suggest that neither model scaling nor naive agent chaining suffices, and that closing the loop demands explicit physical grounding. PCFBench provides the community with a rigorous, multi-dimensional testbed to measure progress toward AI-assisted photonic engineering. The project is available at https://pcfbench.github.io/.
papers.abstract_zh: 光子晶体光纤（PCF）支撑着电信、传感和高功率激光传输等关键应用，但其设计仍是人工、专家密集的过程，将几何直觉与深奥的波导物理相结合。视觉语言模型（VLM）为自动化 PCF 设计提供了有前景的路径，但它们能否真正从显微图像推理光子物理，还是仅识别视觉模式？我们提出 PCFBench，这是首个评估 VLM 在光子逆向设计循环中感知、推理和决策步骤的综合基准。PCFBench 涵盖 26 个任务，组织为认知需求递增的六个类别（几何感知、物理理解、文本生成、多模态推理、逆向设计决策和代码生成），由跨 18 个结构多样光纤家族的超过 220K 个 FDTD 仿真样本构建。我们既评估单个 VLM 在孤立任务上的表现，也评估多智能体系统（MAS）在从感知到设计的完整顺序流水线上的表现。结果揭示出显著的感知—设计差距：当前模型能以中等成功率识别光纤几何，却始终无法将这种视觉理解转化为物理感知的设计行动。此外，将智能体级联到流水线中会暴露显著的误差传播，上游感知错误会累积为下游设计失败。这些发现表明，模型扩展或朴素智能体链式连接都不足够，闭环需要显式的物理 grounding。PCFBench 为社区提供了一个严格、多维的测试平台，以衡量 AI 辅助光子工程的进展。项目见 https://pcfbench.github.io/。
papers.tldr_zh: PCFBench 基于 18 类光纤家族逾 220K 个 FDTD 样本构建 26 项任务，评估 VLM 与多智能体在光子逆向设计中的表现，发现模型能中等程度识别几何却难以转化为物理感知设计，且存在误差传播。

papers.title: Cycle-of-Thought: Self-Evaluative Iterative Reasoning for Table Visual Question Answering in Document Images
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have significantly improved Visual Question Answering (VQA) performance, yet their reasoning over structured content such as tables remains inconsistent, often plagued by spatial misalignment and logical hallucinations. Existing approaches for improving table VQA typically rely on architectural modifications or expensive supervised fine-tuning (SFT), which impose high barriers to entry due to the need for large-scale, expert-annotated datasets and significant computational resources. In this work, we propose Self-RefineVQA, a training-free, inference-time self-correction framework that improves table VQA performance without additional labeled data or model updates. Inspired by human revision behavior, our method enables a single VLM to iteratively act as a generator, critic, and refiner, forming a closed self-feedback loop that corrects common reasoning errors through prompt-guided re-evaluation. Experiments on tabular VQA benchmarks demonstrate that Self-RefineVQA yields consistent accuracy gains in monolingual and cross-lingual understanding, with a particularly significant boost for small models, enabling lightweight models (e.g., 2B-7B parameters) to rival the performance of significantly larger counterparts. Furthermore, we provide a comparative complexity analysis demonstrating that while inference cost increases linearly, our framework offers superior data efficiency and a lower cumulative cost by eliminating the prohibitive annotation bottleneck of human labeling required for fine-tuning. Our results highlight the potential of prompt-based self-improvement as a scalable, accessible paradigm for reliable table reasoning in VLMs.
papers.abstract_zh: 视觉语言模型（VLM）的最新进展显著提升了视觉问答（VQA）的性能，但其对表格等结构化内容的推理仍不稳定，常受空间错位和逻辑幻觉困扰。现有改进表格 VQA 的方法通常依赖架构修改或昂贵的监督微调（SFT），由于需要大规模专家标注数据集和大量计算资源，入门门槛较高。在本工作中，我们提出 Self-RefineVQA，一个无需训练、在推理时进行自我纠正的框架，无需额外标注数据或模型更新即可提升表格 VQA 性能。受人类修改行为启发，我们的方法使单个 VLM 迭代地充当生成器、批评者和精炼者，形成闭环自我反馈回路，通过提示引导的重新评估来纠正常见推理错误。在表格 VQA 基准上的实验表明，Self-RefineVQA 在单语和跨语言理解中均带来一致的准确率提升，对小模型的提升尤为显著，使轻量模型（如 2B-7B 参数）能够媲美规模大得多的模型。此外，我们提供了复杂度对比分析，表明虽然推理成本线性增加，但该框架具有更优的数据效率，并通过消除微调所需人工标注这一高昂瓶颈而降低了累计成本。我们的结果凸显了基于提示的自我改进作为 VLM 中可靠表格推理的可扩展、易获取范式的潜力。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出无需训练、推理时自我纠正的 Self-RefineVQA 框架，让单个 VLM 迭代充当生成器、批评者和精炼者，在表格 VQA 基准上取得一致准确率提升，并显著增强小模型表现。

papers.title: NgramRL: Accelerating RL Post-Training for Structured Generation via Rollout-Aware N-gram Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but its cost is dominated by autoregressive rollout generation, which can exceed 70% of training time. Existing speculative-decoding methods are poorly suited to this setting: model-based drafters consume scarce GPU memory and may become misaligned as the policy evolves, while existing model-free methods do not explicitly exploit repetition across training epochs. We observe that recent rollouts of the same prompt provide a high-quality, self-updating draft source. Based on this insight, we propose NgramRL, a per-prompt n-gram drafter constructed from bounded recent rollout history. NgramRL requires no auxiliary model, drafter training, or persistent GPU-resident drafter state, while target-model verification preserves the rollout distribution. To hide CPU cache lookup and scheduling, we further introduce an adaptive fan-out prefetcher that predicts likely verification outcomes (j, b), consisting of the accepted draft length j and target-emitted continuation token b. A causal budget allocator concentrates prefetches on high-probability outcomes, while uncovered outcomes fall back to sequential lookup without changing committed tokens. Across two model families and three reasoning and structured-generation workloads, NgramRL commits 3.60-7.77 tokens per target-model forward in the warm-cache regime, up to 1.99x more than SuffixDecoding and 7.0x more than prompt-lookup decoding. On Spider, the prefetcher covers 96.6% of Qwen3-8B outcomes at a candidate budget of 16 and improves measured rollout throughput by 1.38x over synchronous NgramRL, approaching its 1.40x overlap ceiling.
papers.abstract_zh: 强化学习（RL）后训练提升了大语言模型的推理能力，但其成本主要来自自回归 rollout 生成，可超过训练时间的 70%。现有推测解码方法难以适配这一场景：基于模型的草稿器占用稀缺 GPU 内存，且可能随策略演化而失配；现有免模型方法则未显式利用跨训练轮次的重复。我们观察到，同一提示的近期 rollout 提供了高质量、可自我更新的草稿来源。基于此洞察，我们提出 NgramRL，一种由有界近期 rollout 历史构建的按提示 n-gram 草稿器。NgramRL 无需辅助模型、草稿器训练或常驻 GPU 的草稿器状态，同时目标模型验证保持 rollout 分布不变。为隐藏 CPU 缓存查找与调度开销，我们进一步引入自适应扇出预取器，预测可能的验证结果 (j, b)，即接受的草稿长度 j 和目标模型输出的续接 token b。因果预算分配器将预取集中于高概率结果，未覆盖的结果回退到顺序查找而不改变已提交 token。在两个模型家族和三个推理与结构化生成工作负载上，NgramRL 在热缓存条件下每次目标模型前向提交 3.60-7.77 个 token，比 SuffixDecoding 最多高 1.99 倍，比 prompt-lookup decoding 高 7.0 倍。在 Spider 上，预取器在候选预算为 16 时覆盖 Qwen3-8B 的 96.6% 结果，并将实测 rollout 吞吐较同步 NgramRL 提升 1.38 倍，接近其 1.40 倍的重叠上限。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 NgramRL，利用同一提示近期 rollout 历史构建按提示 n-gram 草稿器并配合自适应预取，在无需辅助模型的情况下加速 RL 后训练的 rollout 生成，热缓存下每次前向提交 3.60-7.77 个 token。

papers.title: Multimodal Generative AI Assists Comprehensive Echocardiographic Interpretation
papers.abstract_en: Echocardiography is the cornerstone of cardiovascular diagnostics, yet its global utility is constrained by a critical shortage of experienced interpreters. Current artificial intelligence (AI) solutions remain limited, typically operating as opaque "black boxes" or focusing on narrow tasks that fail to capture the holistic, guideline-driven reasoning of a clinician. Here we introduce EchoChat, a generative multimodal vision-language model that performs comprehensive echocardiographic analysis to support clinician interpretation. By emulating the cognitive workflow of a cardiologist, EchoChat integrates vast medical knowledge with a chain-of-thought reasoning mechanism to explicitly ground its conclusions in visual evidence. Trained on echocardiography-instruction pairs from 46,358 examinations, our model establishes a new state-of-the-art across diverse cohorts from six international medical centers. It supports the broadest diagnostic scope of 33 cardiac conditions and findings, including 15 newly added conditions for which it achieves an average F1 of 73.7% across available external evaluations. It surpasses existing best-performing foundation models in cardiac condition recognition (improving average recall by 13.54% on shared tasks) and quantification (average R2 score increase of 0.275 on shared tasks). Furthermore, in a source-blinded echocardiographer reader study, echocardiography reports co-generated with EchoChat were rated higher in diagnostic accuracy and completeness by two senior echocardiographers, and improved diagnostic performance from 72.78% to 82.75% in terms of F1 score over routine-reader only reports. These results demonstrate that integrating clinical reasoning into multimodal AI can democratize specialist expertise and transform the standard of cardiovascular care.
papers.abstract_zh: 超声心动图是心血管诊断的基石，但全球应用受限于经验丰富的解读人员严重短缺。当前人工智能（AI）方案仍然有限，通常表现为不透明的“黑箱”，或聚焦于狭窄任务，无法捕捉临床医生整体性、指南驱动的推理。在此，我们提出 EchoChat，一个生成式多模态视觉语言模型，执行全面的超声心动图分析以支持临床医生解读。通过模拟心脏病专家的认知工作流，EchoChat 将大量医学知识与思维链推理机制相结合，使其结论明确地基于视觉证据。在来自 46,358 次检查的超声心动图指令对上训练后，我们的模型在来自六个国际医疗中心的不同队列上建立了新的最先进水平。它支持最广泛的 33 种心脏状况与发现的诊断范围，其中包括 15 种新增状况，在可用的外部评估中平均 F1 达 73.7%。它在心脏状况识别（共享任务上平均召回率提升 13.54%）和量化（共享任务上平均 R2 分数提升 0.275）方面超越了现有最佳基础模型。此外，在一项来源盲法的超声心动图医师阅读研究中，两位资深超声心动图医师对与 EchoChat 共同生成的超声心动图报告在诊断准确性和完整性上评分更高，且相较仅常规读者报告，F1 分数从 72.78% 提升至 82.75%。这些结果表明，将临床推理融入多模态 AI 可使专家知识普及化并改变心血管护理标准。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出生成式多模态视觉语言模型 EchoChat，基于 46,358 次检查的指令对训练并结合思维链推理，在六个国际中心队列上实现 33 种心脏状况诊断的最先进水平，并在医师阅读研究中提升报告质量与诊断 F1。

papers.title: Lifelong Context Adaptation through Bidirectional Memory-Skill Learning
papers.abstract_en: Lifelong LLM agents must learn from an expanding history of interactions while making each decision within a bounded context window. Memory makes past experience available, but the agent may still need to infer how to solve each new task from the retrieved records. Skills provide reusable procedures, yet may omit the task-specific facts needed to apply them. Because retrieved memory and skills shape the agent's behavior, they also influence the experience available for future learning. We introduce MemCryst, a framework for lifelong context adaptation through bidirectional learning of memory and skills with a frozen language model. Recurring episodes stored in memory support skill creation and revision, and the interactions guided by those skills supply new memory for subsequent learning. Facts retrieved from memory and learned skills jointly form the agent's context, while task outcomes adjust the future retrieval influence of the records actually served without rewriting their content. Across ten settings spanning embodied control, long-document reading, conversation, mathematics, and code, MemCryst leads seven reported comparisons. On ALFWorld, joint serving achieves 63.17% success, compared with 59.83% for memory-only and 50.50% for skill-only serving. Code is available at https://github.com/tianyi0216/Memcryst.git
papers.abstract_zh: 终身 LLM 智能体必须从不断扩展的交互历史中学习，同时在有限上下文窗口内做出每个决策。记忆使过去经验可用，但智能体可能仍需从检索记录中推断如何解决每个新任务。技能提供可复用流程，却可能遗漏应用所需的任务特定事实。由于检索到的记忆和技能塑造智能体行为，它们也影响未来学习可用的经验。我们提出 MemCryst，一个在冻结语言模型下通过记忆与技能双向学习实现终身上下文适应的框架。存储在记忆中的重复片段支持技能创建与修订，而这些技能引导的交互又为后续学习提供新记忆。从记忆检索的事实与习得技能共同构成智能体上下文，任务结果则调整实际提供记录的未来检索影响力，而不重写其内容。在涵盖具身控制、长文档阅读、对话、数学和代码的十个设置中，MemCryst 在七项报告比较中领先。在 ALFWorld 上，联合提供达到 63.17% 成功率，而仅记忆为 59.83%，仅技能为 50.50%。代码见 https://github.com/tianyi0216/Memcryst.git。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 MemCryst 框架，在冻结语言模型下通过记忆与技能的双向学习实现终身上下文适应，在十个设置中七项领先，ALFWorld 上联合提供记忆与技能达 63.17% 成功率。

papers.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms
papers.abstract_en: Adversarial sharpness penalty per iteration of a base optimizer, known as sharpness-aware minimization (SAM), is an accepted technique to improve generalization in deep learning. Recently, Muon has emerged as a dominant optimization algorithm for training large language models (LLMs). It achieves lower sample complexity for heavy-tailed gradient updates - a phenomenon common in LLM training. However, sharpness penalties with Muon updates are yet largely unexplored in the literature. Moreover, the behavior of SAM under heavy-tailed noise is unknown both theoretically and empirically. A potential reason for this gap is the additional cost of extra gradient computation per iteration for penalty perturbations in SAM, which becomes prohibitive for LLMs. This paper introduces Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithm (SOMA) to combine a computationally efficient and theoretically grounded perturbation scheme with the Muon algorithm. The key idea is to use stale (purely) stochastic gradient noise for adversarial perturbations. Theoretically, we show that SOMA's sample complexity is invariant to the perturbation direction. We provide explorations and insights into SOMA's robustness to heavy-tailed gradient noise. We extensively explore SOMA's efficacy in (a) mitigating quality degradation due to post-training quantization, and (b) catastrophic forgetting during fine-tuning of LLMs.
papers.abstract_zh: 基础优化器每次迭代的对抗性锐度惩罚，即锐度感知最小化（SAM），是提升深度学习泛化能力的公认技术。近来，Muon 已成为训练大语言模型（LLM）的主流优化算法。它对重尾梯度更新实现了更低的样本复杂度——这是 LLM 训练中常见的现象。然而，结合 Muon 更新的锐度惩罚在文献中仍基本未被探索。此外，SAM 在重尾噪声下的行为在理论和实证上均未知。这一空白的一个可能原因是 SAM 中惩罚扰动每次迭代需额外梯度计算，这对 LLM 而言变得难以承受。本文提出锐度感知正交化动量算法（SOMA），将计算高效且有理论依据的扰动方案与 Muon 算法相结合。关键思想是使用陈旧（纯）随机梯度噪声进行对抗扰动。理论上，我们证明 SOMA 的样本复杂度对扰动方向不变。我们提供对 SOMA 在重尾梯度噪声下鲁棒性的探索与洞见。我们广泛探索 SOMA 在以下方面的有效性：(a) 缓解训练后量化导致的质量退化，(b) LLM 微调期间的灾难性遗忘。
papers.tldr_zh: 提出 SOMA，将基于陈旧随机梯度噪声的高效扰动方案与 Muon 优化器结合，理论上证明样本复杂度对扰动方向不变，并探索其在缓解训练后量化质量退化和微调灾难性遗忘方面的效果。

papers.title: Green Code or Costly Code? Evaluating the Energy Costs of Iterative LLM-Based Code Optimizations
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used to optimize code for performance. This practice often assumes that improvements in execution speed naturally translate into overall lower energy consumption. We challenge this assumption empirically by measuring whether performance-optimized code produced by LLM self-refinement pipelines is also energy-efficient relative to canonical human reference solutions, and whether the energy cost of the optimization process can be offset by subsequent execution-time savings. We evaluate 11 open-source models across four decoding configurations on all 1,000 problems of EffiBench, a state-of-the-art performance benchmark, while collecting per-process, hardware-level energy measurements throughout. Inference energy spans 0.79 to 8.68 MJ across model-variant pairs, which is roughly equivalent to the energy of 250 to 2800 GPT-4.1 queries. Limiting the maximum number of output tokens has the largest impact, reducing energy use by up to 69% compared to the default configuration. On the execution side, 42 of 44 configurations produce code that consumes more energy per problem than the canonical human reference, with overheads ranging from +4% to +886%. The two exceptions achieve only marginal gains, with break-even points on the order of 10^6 to 10^7 executions. Mixture-of-Experts architectures consume substantially less inference energy than equivalently-sized dense models without sacrificing correctness, making architectural choice a more consequential sustainability lever than decoding parameters. Performance optimization and energy efficiency are not always aligned goals: LLM self-refinement consistently produces faster-seeking but energy-heavier code relative to what a human engineer would write. All artifacts are available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23598170.
papers.abstract_zh: 大语言模型（LLM）越来越多地被用于优化代码性能。这种做法通常假设执行速度的提升会自然转化为整体能耗的降低。我们通过实证测量挑战这一假设：由 LLM 自我精炼流程生成的性能优化代码，相对于规范的人工参考解是否同样节能，以及优化过程本身的能耗能否被后续执行时的节能所抵消。我们在 EffiBench（一个先进的性能基准）的全部 1,000 道问题上，评估了 11 个开源模型在四种解码配置下的表现，并全程采集逐进程的硬件级能耗测量。不同模型-变体组合的推理能耗跨度从 0.79 到 8.68 MJ，大致相当于 250 到 2800 次 GPT-4.1 查询的能耗。限制最大输出 token 数影响最大，相比默认配置可将能耗降低最多 69%。在执行侧，44 种配置中有 42 种生成的代码在每个问题上比规范人工参考解消耗更多能量，额外开销从 +4% 到 +886% 不等。仅有的两个例外也只取得边际收益，其盈亏平衡点约为 10^6 到 10^7 次执行。混合专家（MoE）架构的推理能耗显著低于同等规模的稠密模型，且不牺牲正确性，这使得架构选择成为比解码参数更具影响力的可持续性杠杆。性能优化与能效并不总是对齐的目标：相对于人类工程师会写出的代码，LLM 自我精炼持续生成追求更快但能耗更高的代码。所有工件见 https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23598170。
papers.tldr_zh: 在 EffiBench 全部 1,000 题上测量 11 个开源模型的 LLM 自我精炼代码优化流程，发现 44 种配置中 42 种生成的代码比人工参考解能耗高 4% 至 886%，且优化过程推理能耗达 0.79–8.68 MJ，性能优化与能效并不一致。

papers.title: Efficient Zero-Shot Video Anomaly Detection via Signal-Aware Adaptive Fusion (SAAF)
papers.abstract_en: Deploying Vision-Language Models for video anomaly detection confronts a fundamental constraint. Their semantic reasoning demands computational budgets incompatible with the scale of real-world video streams. We present Signal-Aware Adaptive Fusion (SAAF), a framework that achieves efficient zero-shot anomaly detection through three key innovations. First, we introduce a dual-signal adaptive sampler operating in semantic embedding space: a delta signal captures sudden events via frame-to-frame cosine distance, while a drift signal detects static and gradual anomalies through deviation from rolling temporal context. Their OR-gated combination with adaptive EMA-based thresholding provides comprehensive anomaly coverage without training data. Second, we propose a threshold-gated cascaded architecture where lightweight frame-level scoring precedes expensive video-level temporal analysis, invoking it only when confidence warrants additional context. Third, we design a signal-aware weighted fusion mechanism that dynamically adapts score combination based on which signal triggered frame selection. Across four benchmarks, SAAF delivers competitive accuracy at substantially lower cost. Among training-free zero-shot methods, SAAF sets a new state of the art on XD-Violence (92.07%), MSAD (86.70%), and ShanghaiTech (80.54%) AUC-ROC, with XD-Violence and MSAD also surpassing supervised baselines. SAAF sustains 44.95, 48.61, and 41.06 FPS on XD-Violence, UCF-Crime, and MSAD, a 2.43$\times$, 2.63$\times$, and 2.22$\times$ throughput improvement over the prior best zero-shot method. Code: https://github.com/kdawoud91/SAAF
papers.abstract_zh: 将视觉-语言模型用于视频异常检测面临一个根本性约束：其语义推理所需的计算预算与真实世界视频流的规模不相容。我们提出信号感知自适应融合（SAAF），一个通过三项关键创新实现高效零样本异常检测的框架。第一，我们引入在语义嵌入空间中运行的双信号自适应采样器：delta 信号通过帧间余弦距离捕捉突发事件，drift 信号通过偏离滚动时间上下文检测静态和渐变异常；二者以 OR 门控组合并配合基于 EMA 的自适应阈值，无需训练数据即可提供全面的异常覆盖。第二，我们提出阈值门控的级联架构，轻量级帧级评分先于昂贵的视频级时间分析，仅在置信度表明需要额外上下文时才调用后者。第三，我们设计信号感知加权融合机制，根据触发帧选择的信号动态调整分数组合方式。在四个基准上，SAAF 以显著更低的成本取得有竞争力的准确率。在免训练零样本方法中，SAAF 在 XD-Violence（92.07%）、MSAD（86.70%）和 ShanghaiTech（80.54%）AUC-ROC 上刷新最优结果，其中 XD-Violence 和 MSAD 还超过了有监督基线。SAAF 在 XD-Violence、UCF-Crime 和 MSAD 上分别保持 44.95、48.61 和 41.06 FPS，相比此前最佳零样本方法吞吐量分别提升 2.43 倍、2.63 倍和 2.22 倍。代码：https://github.com/kdawoud91/SAAF
papers.tldr_zh: SAAF 通过语义嵌入空间中的 delta/drift 双信号自适应采样、阈值门控级联架构与信号感知加权融合，实现免训练零样本视频异常检测，在 XD-Violence、MSAD、ShanghaiTech 上取得 92.07%、86.70%、80.54% AUC-ROC 并显著提升吞吐量。

papers.title: LeafSkill: Efficient Leaf-Level Action Grounding for Recursive LLM Agents
papers.abstract_en: Recursive large language model (LLM) agents solve long-horizon tasks through decomposition, execution, and environmental feedback. Yet after producing an atomic subtask, they often invoke the same large model again to translate a familiar instruction into an executable action. We observe that high-level planning is task-specific, whereas leaf-level action grounding recurs across tasks and can be checked against environment-admitted actions. We introduce LeafSkill, an external reuse layer that retrieves semantically related grounding experience, binds action templates to current objects and admissible actions, and uses a lightweight 1.7B selector to choose a bound action or defer the unchanged subtask to the original agent. Skills remain outside the model parameters, allowing a frozen selector to use post-training additions. Under lexical and syntactic paraphrases, exact matching retrieves none of the reference actions, while semantic retrieval preserves 96.0% and 97.0% candidate coverage; the frozen selector adopts 97.34% of unseen skill types. On an independent confirmation set of 200 Robotouille tasks, LeafSkill completes 137 tasks versus 121 for ReCAP (68.5% vs. 60.5%, exact McNemar p=.0259). On the 106 tasks completed by both, it reduces Qwen3.5-27B tokens by 14.42% and calls by 14.08%. A separate held-out repeat yields a consistent 9.0-point success gain and 18.98% token reduction. Reusable leaf grounding can thus improve task completion while reducing host-model inference without replacing high-level planning.
papers.abstract_zh: 递归大语言模型（LLM）智能体通过分解、执行和环境反馈来解决长时程任务。然而在产生原子子任务之后，它们常常再次调用同一个大模型，把熟悉的指令翻译为可执行动作。我们观察到高层规划是任务特定的，而叶级动作接地会跨任务重复出现，并且可以对照环境允许的动作进行检查。我们提出 LeafSkill，一个外部复用层，它检索语义相关的接地经验，将动作模板绑定到当前对象和允许的动作，并使用轻量级 1.7B 选择器来选择绑定动作或将未改动的子任务交还给原智能体。技能保留在模型参数之外，使冻结的选择器能够使用训练后新增的技能。在词汇和句法改写下，精确匹配检索不到任何参考动作，而语义检索保留了 96.0% 和 97.0% 的候选覆盖；冻结选择器采纳了 97.34% 的未见技能类型。在 200 个 Robotouille 任务的独立确认集上，LeafSkill 完成 137 个任务，而 ReCAP 完成 121 个（68.5% 对 60.5%，精确 McNemar p=.0259）。在两者均完成的 106 个任务上，它将 Qwen3.5-27B 的 token 用量减少 14.42%，调用次数减少 14.08%。另一次留出重复实验得到一致的 9.0 个百分点成功率提升和 18.98% 的 token 减少。因此，可复用的叶级接地可以在不替代高层规划的情况下提升任务完成率并减少宿主模型推理。
papers.tldr_zh: LeafSkill 用外部复用层检索语义相关的叶级动作接地经验并绑定到当前对象与允许动作，由冻结的 1.7B 选择器决定采纳或交还原智能体，在 Robotouille 上以 68.5% 对 60.5% 的成功率超过 ReCAP，并减少约 14% 的 token 与调用次数。

papers.title: Adaptive Control of Scientific Instruments with Nonstationary Responses through Multimodal Agents
papers.abstract_en: Controlling scientific instruments requires parameters to be adjusted progressively in response to feedback from successive operations. When unobserved operating conditions evolve with operational history, responses become nonstationary, and a static mapping from actions to responses becomes inadequate for decisions across shots. Shot-to-shot tuning of neutral beam injection (NBI) ion sources in magnetic confinement fusion devices is representative of this class of problems: the conditions of electrode surfaces and vacuum are difficult to observe directly, discharge outcomes vary between shots, and experiments are costly and carry operational risks. We propose a physically grounded multimodal agent with three independently auditable components. Deterministic algorithms extract symbolic physical quantities and visual evidence from multichannel waveforms; a memory with two layers organizes trajectories from the current task, experience from earlier tasks, and procedural knowledge, from which a multimodal large language model (MLLM) generates candidate actions; and an independent action feasibility check enforces action constraints before execution. In a strictly chronological replay of 455 shots from four EXL-50U platforms, physical symbols alone outperformed waveform images alone by 0.21-0.32 in macro-F1 for quality classification across all four evaluated models. Retrieved context increased the mean agreement with historical action directions by 22.4-42.7 percentage points, whereas the contribution of visual evidence varied across models. Under supervised operation on five ion sources, the system achieved a beam-extraction rate of 86.80% across 409 executed shots. These results demonstrate the engineering feasibility of the framework for supervised sequential tuning on a physical scientific instrument.
papers.abstract_zh: 控制科学仪器需要根据连续操作的反馈逐步调整参数。当未观测到的运行条件随操作历史演变时，响应会变得非平稳，静态的动作到响应映射不足以支撑跨炮次的决策。磁约束聚变装置中中性束注入（NBI）离子源的逐炮调谐是这类问题的代表：电极表面和真空条件难以直接观测，放电结果在炮次之间变化，且实验成本高并伴随运行风险。我们提出一个具有三个可独立审计组件的物理接地多模态智能体。确定性算法从多通道波形中提取符号物理量和视觉证据；一个具有两层的记忆组织当前任务的轨迹、早期任务的经验以及程序性知识，多模态大语言模型（MLLM）据此生成候选动作；独立的动作可行性检查在执行前强制动作约束。在对来自四个 EXL-50U 平台的 455 个炮次进行严格按时间顺序的回放中，在所有四个被评估模型上，仅使用物理符号在质量分类的宏 F1 上比仅使用波形图像高 0.21–0.32。检索到的上下文使与历史动作方向的平均一致率提高 22.4–42.7 个百分点，而视觉证据的贡献因模型而异。在五个离子源上的监督运行中，系统在 409 个已执行炮次上达到 86.80% 的束引出率。这些结果证明了该框架在物理科学仪器上进行监督式顺序调谐的工程可行性。

papers.title: On-Policy Self-Training: Data-Free Self-Improvement in Large Language Models
papers.abstract_en: On-policy self-distillation enables post-training foundation models without relying on stronger external teachers. However, existing approaches rely on ground-truth question-answer pairs, human-curated problem sets, or other supervised signals. In this work, we reformulate on-policy self-distillation as a self-training framework, driven by self-generated question-answer pairs and privileged reasoning demonstrations. We push supervision to the limit: guided solely by coarse, high-level topic descriptions, the model synthesizes its own curriculum of queries and privileged reasoning traces without access to any human-curated prompts or answers. We find that self-distillation on fully synthetic privileged information enables a model to improve across multiple domains while retaining its capabilities on domains it is not self-trained on. We demonstrate the generality of this framework across text and multimodal domains, achieving consistent self-improvement on standard language benchmarks and Visual Question Answering. Our findings demonstrate that foundation models possess rich latent capabilities that can be amplified without external task supervision or curated problem distributions.

papers.title: PROVE: Probabilistic Visual Grounding via Patch-Level Evidence for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Visual grounding with vision-language models such as CLIP typically produces a single deterministic relevance map for an image-query pair, without indicating whether the localisation is reliable or whether the referent is present at all. We introduce \textbf{PROVE} (\textbf{Pro}babilistic \textbf{V}isual Grounding via Patch-Level \textbf{E}vidence), a post-hoc evidential adapter that maps frozen CLIP patch features to per-patch Beta distributions without modifying the backbone. PROVE casts grounding as per-patch membership: each patch accumulates positive and negative evidence for whether it belongs to the referent, so a query may match zero, one, or many patches. We train PROVE with an evidential objective on soft patch-coverage targets, and define a prior-pull objective that keeps absent-referent examples near an uninformative prior, so that vacuity serves as an absence signal without a dedicated presence classifier. During inference, a single forward pass yields, in closed form, a posterior-mean grounding map, a spatial vacuity map, and an image-level absence score. We evaluate PROVE on referring-expression benchmarks: it is competitive in localisation with state-of-the-art CLIP grounding methods, its uncertainty tracks localisation error and supports selective prediction under abstention, and its image-level score detects when the referent is absent altogether. Our evidential patch-membership modelling offers a simple, drop-in mechanism for probabilistic verification in frozen vision-language grounding systems.

papers.title: AlphaAnything: Extending Pretrained RGB Generators to RGBA
papers.abstract_en: Existing RGBA generation methods commonly learn a transparency-specific representation through reconstruction, introducing an additional training stage and potentially altering the RGB decoding function inherited from pretrained models. We present AlphaAnything, a lightweight framework that extends pretrained RGB generators to RGBA directly in their original latent space, without RGBA reconstruction pretraining. AlphaAnything inserts LoRA modules into the generative transformer and attaches an alpha branch to the frozen RGB VAE decoder. Unidirectional RGB-to-alpha feature sharing allows opacity supervision to shape the generative latent while guaranteeing that, for any fixed latent, RGB decoding remains identical to that of the pretrained decoder. We further introduce Endpoint-Aware Alpha Loss (EA Loss), which derives opacity supervision from the complementary foreground--background weights used in compositing. It supports exact opacity endpoints and continuous partial transparency while emphasizing localized alpha errors. Experiments on text-to-RGBA and image-to-RGBA tasks across multiple pretrained RGB backbones demonstrate competitive generation quality, and controlled ablations validate the shared-latent training design and EA Loss.

papers.title: DT-JEPA: Learning to Predict Future Representations for Decision-Making
papers.abstract_en: Decision Transformer (DT) has demonstrated strong performance in various offline reinforcement learning (RL) tasks by conditioning action generation on expected future returns and historical trajectories. However, treating expected future returns as the condition provides an incomplete description of the future, as trajectories with different state transitions and behaviors may share similar returns. Moreover, expected future returns inherently depend on task-specific reward functions, which makes policy learning reliant on reward-labeled datasets and restricts its scalability to tasks with similar but unseen rewards. Recently, Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPA) have emerged as a promising paradigm of self-supervised learning-based world models, which learn predictive representations of future dynamics in latent space rather than reconstructing future states in the original space. Inspired by JEPA, we propose DT-JEPA, an offline pretraining and online fine-tuning framework that learns general knowledge from reward-free offline trajectories and achieves excellent adaptation to unseen tasks. Instead of predicting a single deterministic future embedding, we design a novel probabilistic predictor to model the conditional distribution of future representations in the latent space, thereby capturing both predictive information and uncertainty about future dynamics. Theoretically, we show that 1) the JEPA objective seeks to maximize a variational lower bound on the mutual information between historical representations and future trajectories; and 2) predictive future-conditioned policy learning admits a finite-sample performance bound with an O(N-1/4) estimation term. Experiments on D4RL benchmarks demonstrate that DT-JEPA achieves efficient adaptation across varying offline RL tasks, outperforming traditional DT-based and other offline RL methods.

papers.title: MiD-VLM: Detecting and Grounding Global Semantic Misinformation in Image-Caption Pairs
papers.abstract_en: Semantic misinformation can arise when an authentic image is paired with a caption that changes or distorts its narrative. Because the image itself may contain no visible signs of manipulation, methods designed to detect pixel-level artifacts can miss these misleading image-caption pairs. We study this problem using DGM4+, a dataset designed to evaluate the detection of global scene and semantic inconsistencies. We propose a multimodal model that combines image-text representations from SigLIP with visual scene features from DINOv2 through a projection MLP, and adapts Qwen2-VL-7B using LoRA. The model jointly predicts whether an image-caption pair is authentic, identifies the manipulation type, and grounds the misleading caption tokens. On the DGM4+ validation split, the model achieves an F1 score of $0.9679$ for binary authenticity classification. These results suggest that parameter-efficient adaptation of vision-language models is promising for detecting semantic inconsistencies, while also motivating further work on precise token-level grounding.

papers.title: Solvent: Long-Horizon Reasoning for Multi-Step Retrosynthesis
papers.abstract_en: Multi-step retrosynthesis requires recursively transforming a target molecule through successive reaction steps into purchasable building blocks, and recent work has begun to draw on large language model (LLM) reasoning to tackle the task. In its latest evolution, LLM reasoning has entered the long-horizon regime: models pursue objectives across interdependent steps, interact with environments, and adapt to feedback. This shift has markedly advanced LLM capabilities, as illustrated by breakthroughs in AI-driven mathematical research. At this frontier, we introduce Solvent, an 8B LLM that successfully extends long-horizon reasoning to multi-step retrosynthesis. Through a two-round post-training curriculum, Solvent learns to interleave iterative synthesis planning, external availability verification, and adaptive route revision. Experiments show that, following a $2.1\times$ performance boost from RL, Solvent scores 61.86% across four benchmarks, surpassing mid-scale language models and prior search-based retrosynthesis systems, and rivaling frontier trillion-parameter LLMs.

papers.title: Beyond Post-Hoc Rewards: Privileged Reasoning Exploration for Multimodal Embeddings
papers.abstract_en: Advances in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have driven substantial progress in multimodal embeddings. Recent methods exploit generative capabilities by augmenting embedded inputs with self-generated reasoning to produce more informative embeddings. However, conventional retrieval supervision for training embedding models specifies pairwise relevance relations without explicitly guiding the reasoning used for input augmentation. Such reasoning is neither directly observed nor uniquely determined by the input, allowing multiple plausible traces to introduce semantic cues of varying retrieval utility. Existing approaches largely optimize reasoning conditioned on the input alone, limiting the exploration of retrieval-relevant traces. We introduce PILOT, a framework that models reasoning as a latent variable and instantiates its prior and posterior distributions as distinct reasoning modes of a shared MLLM. The prior conditions only on the input, whereas the posterior uses additional training-time relational evidence to guide reasoning exploration. To translate the posterior's broader exploration into inference-time improvements, we derive an importance-weighted variational objective and instantiate it as a prior-posterior co-evolution framework that improves both modes under a shared inference-compatible reward while selectively transferring posterior trajectories to the prior according to their utility and prior reachability. On the 78-task MMEB-V2 benchmark, PILOT outperforms the primary baseline across all 12 task groups at both 2B and 7B parameters, improving overall scores by 3.2 and 3.3 points, respectively, with the largest gains in visual-document retrieval (+6.1 and +6.4 points). Our results show that relational supervision is most valuable not as a post-hoc reward but as a signal for shaping how reasoning is explored in training reasoning-enhanced embedding models.

papers.title: Organizing Temporal Evidence in Hyperbolic Space for Video Moment Retrieval
papers.abstract_en: Video moment retrieval aims to localize a query-relevant temporal segment in an untrimmed video. Existing methods typically perform video-text alignment in Euclidean space, where representations are embedded in a flat geometry. However, accurate moment localization requires organizing query-relevant evidence across multiple grounding states, where target regions, boundary transitions, and contextual distractors exhibit distinct temporal structures and relevance patterns. Such Euclidean representations lack an explicit geometry to jointly capture these relationships, motivating us to explore structured temporal evidence organization from a geometric perspective. Specifically, we propose Hyperbolic Temporal Evidence Organization (HTEO), a geometric framework that organizes query-aware temporal memory in hyperbolic space. HTEO maps temporal representations into a Poincaré ball and organizes temporal evidence through Radial Evidence Organization (REO) and Orthogonal Angular Refinement (OAR). REO adjusts temporal tokens' radial positions to encode the structural differences among temporal evidence, while OAR enhances query-conditioned semantic alignment through orthogonal rotation. The organized representation is then projected back to the Euclidean tangent space and injected into the decoder through a lightweight residual memory update, enabling hyperbolic geometric cues to be incorporated into standard Transformer decoders while preserving the original cross-modal memory. Furthermore, we introduce radial structure regularization and angular relevance supervision to explicitly guide temporal evidence organization and query-conditioned semantic alignment, respectively. Extensive experiments and analyses across multiple benchmarks demonstrate that HTEO improves temporal localization while providing an interpretable geometric organization of temporal evidence.

papers.title: Residual Expert Routing for Text-Only Domain Adaptation of Factorized Transducer ASR
papers.abstract_en: Fine-tuning the non-blank predictor of a factorized transducer on target-domain text improves recognition on that domain but degrades performance on the source domain. A single interpolation weight between base and adapted predictors cannot resolve this: the adapted predictor helps at some prefixes and hurts at others, often within one utterance. We propose conservative residual routing: the adapted predictor becomes a residual correction to the base, and a 16k-parameter gate decides at each prefix how much of it to admit. Closing the gate reproduces the base exactly. On a 40-hour conversational corpus, routing retains essentially all of the text-only gain on two held-out domains (19.89 to 16.74, 20.91 to 16.21 WER) while leaving source-domain WER unchanged (12.90 to 12.93); the adapted predictor alone costs 1.08 WER. Routing needs no per-domain tuning on target-domain audio. Analysis reveals the gate does not behave as a simple domain-level switch: it modulates intervention through the disagreement between the two predictors, suppressing it in-domain and amplifying it out-of-domain.

papers.title: Search-Based Testing of Modality Sensitivity in Vision Language Models
papers.abstract_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) process images and text jointly, yet robustness evaluations often perturb these inputs separately or assess only predefined corruption levels. Such evaluations provide limited evidence of which modality is more susceptible to perturbations and whether smaller changes across both modalities can jointly expose failures. We present MoST, a black-box testing framework that characterizes modality sensitivity by comparing image-only, text-only, and joint perturbations. MoST uses multi-objective search to select and combine perturbations and adjust their severity, seeking prediction degradation while limiting changes to images and prompts. We evaluate MoST on four VLMs performing object localization on ImageNet and driving images. The models exhibit distinct sensitivities: textual perturbations dominate for some, whereas others are susceptible across both modalities. In several configurations, joint perturbations match or exceed the effectiveness of single-modality perturbations with smaller modifications to each input. In a human study, 60-76% of assessments across models judge the perturbed inputs sufficiently understandable to perform the task, and human localization is more accurate than that of the corresponding VLMs. These results show that evaluating modalities separately can overlook failure-inducing combinations and that modality sensitivity provides a more detailed account of VLM robustness than aggregate failure rates alone.

papers.title: ViT-H: Generative Video-To-Humanoid Control with Motion Tracking Feedback
papers.abstract_en: Learning humanoid control from monocular human videos offers a scalable way to acquire diverse whole-body behaviors. Yet, existing reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines are limited in system-level scalability by separately optimized intermediate stages and cannot directly optimize reference motion executability using downstream tracking feedback. We present ViT-H, a video-to-humanoid control framework following a generation-and-tracking paradigm. ViT-H directly generates humanoid reference motions from videos with a diffusion model, bypassing human motion reconstruction and retargeting, and uses motion-tracking outcomes to post-train the generator with direct preference optimization. We further introduce an autoregressive variant that enables real-time humanoid video teleoperation with sub-400 ms latency. Extensive experiments on the Unitree G1 demonstrate that ViT-H outperforms state-of-the-art reconstruction-retargeting-tracking pipelines in both motion quality and executability. We further show that ViT-H scales favorably with model size and with both pre-training and post-training data scale, while motion-tracking feedback consistently improves executability across different motion trackers.

papers.title: Do Language Models Trust Their Own Justifications? A Study on Functional Consistency
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) have been widely adopted in text classification tasks, where they not only output class predictions but also generate explanations that highlight the tokens deemed most relevant for reaching the predicted label. Yet it remains unclear whether these highlighted elements are behaviorally consistent with the model's own predictions under targeted interventions, which we refer to as functional auto-consistency. While much of the literature evaluates the textual plausibility of such explanations, few studies assess their functional consistency with the model's actual behavior. In this work, we propose an experimental framework based on the principle of auto-consistency: if a model identifies certain tokens as decisive, then isolating, removing, or semantically inverting them should produce systematic and interpretable changes in its predictions. We operationalize this evaluation through sufficiency, comprehensiveness, and counterfactuality metrics, and conduct experiments on IMDB and Steam reviews across both closed-source (GPT-4o-mini) and open-source LLMs (Gemma3, Granite8B, DeepSeek). Results show that GPT-4o-mini follows the expected progression across all metrics, Gemma3 and Granite8B maintain coherence under sufficiency but lose consistency under more demanding interventions, while DeepSeek variants display structural deviations, either failing to preserve sufficiency or overreacting under comprehensiveness and counterfactuality. These findings show that explanation reliability varies across LLM families and scales, with smaller models displaying contradictions and larger ones exhibiting over-sensitivity. By combining sufficiency, comprehensiveness, and counterfactuality, our approach provides a systematic methodology for assessing the functional consistency of LLM self-explanations.

papers.title: ARENA: Active Region attENtion Aggregation for interpretable solar flare prediction
papers.abstract_en: Predicting solar flares is a challenging space-weather forecasting problem with potentially significant impacts on Earth's upper atmosphere, including disruptions to radio communications. We propose Active Region attENtion Aggregation (ARENA), a neural network architecture that predicts solar flares from a variable number of active-region cutouts while learning to identify the region most relevant to the prediction. ARENA is trained using multiple-instance learning under weak supervision, requiring only a flare/no-flare label for the observation and no labels specifying the flare origin. The learned attention mechanism therefore provides a means of localizing the active region driving the prediction without explicit origin annotations. ARENA achieves a heidke skill score of 0.45 which is comparable to other flare prediction approaches. These results demonstrate that active-region-based aggregation can provide an efficient and interpretable approach to solar flare prediction. The code is available at https://github.com/LuisBauer22/ARENA.

papers.title: The Answer Knows Where to Look: Zooming before MLLMs Answer under Visual-Token Budgets
papers.abstract_en: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) read images through visual tokens, and under the small per-image budgets that efficient deployment requires, the fine text of documents, charts and infographics becomes illegible. Zooming in recovers the evidence, but the region must be chosen before the model answers. We find that MLLMs know where the evidence is, but not in a form that can be read before they answer: the answer tokens localize it from the middle layers on, whereas the attention available before answering does so only in the top layers, at a depth that varies across models, and diffusely. Supervising the pre-answer attention to point degrades reading, and the benefit of zooming is governed by each image's information gap. Building on these findings, we introduce ours, which lets an MLLM look where its answer would. A dedicated look token, processed in a single prefill and kept out of the answering pass, learns in hindsight to attend as the model's own correct answers do, extracting this knowledge into a concentrated pointer before any answer exists. Its hidden state then selects how to look, from no zoom to crops, square windows, windows that adapt to the pointer and foveated warps, supervised by the counterfactual outcome of every view. ours needs no box annotations, per-model layer search, external localizers or generation before the answer. On Qwen3-VL at three scales and five text-rich benchmarks, it surpasses the strongest baseline by 4.8-9.1 points at 98 visual tokens per view and attention-guided zooming by 11.1-17.0 points, while running faster than attention-guided and grounding-based zooming.

papers.title: Reuse, Don't Retrain: Efficient, Modality-Versatile Geospatial Foundation Models through Feature Distillation
papers.abstract_en: Geospatial foundation models (GeoFMs) are costly to pretrain, yet model families often repeat this process across backbone scales and sensing modalities. We investigate feature distillation as a more efficient way to reuse existing representations. First, we distill frozen CROMA and TerraMind teachers into smaller Vision Transformers through patch-level feature matching. Across nine PANGAEA tasks, distilled TerraMind Tiny, Small, and Base outperform their scale-matched released counterparts by 2.76, 3.02, and 1.87 mean IoU points, respectively; each also matches or exceeds the next-larger released model. Distilled CROMA-Base gains 2.05 points. TerraMind-Base required only 43 A6000 GPU-hours, approximately 0.5\% of the reported cost of independent pretraining. Second, we introduce TEDI, an unpaired multi-expert approach combining TerraMind for multispectral imagery and DINOv3 for high-resolution RGB. Separate patch embeddings route unpaired inputs into a shared Transformer trunk, removing the need for co-registered data. TEDI-Large achieves the highest single-model mean in our PANGAEA-9 comparison (62.51 mIoU), outperforming both teachers overall while retaining their modality-specific strengths. TEDI-Base reaches 61.75 mIoU with 72\% fewer parameters. These results show that distillation improves the GeoFM accuracy-compute frontier while consolidating complementary experts into a single versatile backbone.

papers.title: Sustainability of TSFM Deployment and Pretraining: From Carbon Footprint Analysis to Mitigation via Pruning
papers.abstract_en: Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) offer strong zero-shot forecasting capabilities, but their high pretraining cost raises a practical sustainability question: does this upfront investment pay off over a full deployment lifecycle, compared to supervised standalone models that must be periodically retrained? We model the cumulative carbon cost of different approaches across a realistic industrial scenario: Chronos-2 amortizes its pretraining cost within months for large or frequently queried deployments, but a classical model remains cheaper indefinitely for small or rarely queried ones. For cases where reducing the TSFM's own cost matters, we show that removing a single encoder block (7.9% of parameters) via a gradient-free pruning criterion yields a consistent 6 to 9% reduction in FLOPs, CO2 emissions, and latency, at essentially no cost to zero-shot forecasting performance across a 25-task benchmark.

papers.title: MusicTwins: Training Audio-Language Models to Listen like Their Persona
papers.abstract_en: People differ in how they perceive music, what associations they make with it, what they like about it, and how they respond to it. Computational models intended to simulate people in environments that include music should account for these differences. Although LLMs have been shown to reproduce aspects of human behavior, whether audio-language models (ALMs) can reproduce a specific person's responses to textual and musical stimuli remains underexplored. We introduce MusicTwins, a framework that combines persona summaries, personal memory, and post-training to generate person-specific responses. We construct persona representations from human writings, capturing background, views, personality, writing style, and a musical profile, and post-train Audio Flamingo Next through supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. Evaluation on ten held-out personas shows notable improvements for Audio Flamingo Next in persona fidelity, including personality, writing style, and responses to music, supporting MusicTwins as a foundation for training audio-language models to listen like their persona.

papers.title: LGMT: A Tool for Testing the Logical Reasoning Reliability of LLMs
papers.abstract_en: Large Language Models (LLMs) increasingly serve as reasoning components in modern software systems, yet a model that answers a logical query correctly can contradict itself when the same problem is restated in an equivalent form. papers.title: PathJev: Decision-Native Vision-Language Modelling for Histopathology

papers.title: CauProphet: Teaching Agents to Develop Causal Cognition like Humans
papers.abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly support long-horizon tasks by leveraging external memory and past experience. papers.title: Reading Between the Layers: Cross-Modal Alignment and Representational Hierarchy in Vision Transformers
papers.abstract_en: While large vision-language models excel at optical character recognition, it remains unclear how their underlying vision encoders process text and its meaning, and whether they support anything resembling reading comprehension. Together, our results suggest that increasing model and training-data scale, as well as text-rich training data, can partially compensate for the absence of language supervision.

papers.title: When to Stop Penalizing Actions? Martingale GRPO for VLA Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: A failed vision-language-action (VLA) rollout does not imply that every action contributed to failure. Yet in group-relative policy optimization (GRPO), a single trajectory-level advantage is assigned to all actions in a rollout. Potentially useful recovery attempts can thus be penalized alongside the errors they aim to correct. Ideal stopping conditions for failure feedback are characterized using success-probability and policy-score martingales. At these stops, the removed gradient contribution has zero conditional expectation given the retained information. Truncation therefore preserves the expectation of a reference GRPO group-gradient estimator and can reduce its covariance. One such stop occurs when the conditional probability of success is zero, motivating error and recovery cues for selecting candidate feedback boundaries. Martingale GRPO (MART-GRPO) is introduced with a vision-language model (VLM) for event-guided truncation. The VLM is fine-tuned on our annotated training set using low-rank adaptation (LoRA). The last visible error without observed recovery is localized by the frozen VLM in complete rollout videos. Failure feedback is retained through the selected error interval and removed afterward, while successful-rollout loss terms and original loss normalization are preserved. For retrospective boundaries, changes in expectation and variance are analyzed to assess departures from ideal stopping. Experiments with OpenVLA-OFT on RoboTwin 2.0 show that MART-GRPO improves success rates over full-trajectory GRPO across multiple tasks.

papers.title: A Broader Look into MLLM's Retrieval Heads
papers.abstract_en: Locating relevant evidence in long inputs is a core capability of Multimodal Large Language Models. Prior studies attribute this capability to retrieval heads, a sparse set of attention heads that transfer information from the context to the output. However, these analyses are confined to a limited set of modalities and the corresponding models. Moreover, how retrieval heads can be leveraged to enhance the model calls for further exploration. In this paper, we ask whether this mechanism expands together with the input modalities of the model. Taking audio-visual input as a newly added modality, we construct paired inputs in which the same answer is either spoken or shown on screen. With the evidence content fixed, retrieval heads remain sparse in the new modality and are shared to a large extent across modalities. Across 18 language, vision-language, and omni-modal checkpoints, omni-modal models largely preserve the retrieval heads of their backbones. Ablating these heads eliminates nearly all audio-visual retrieval. The heads shared across modalities make up fewer than 2\% of all heads, yet ablating them also degrades document understanding, spatial perception, and visual mathematics. Building on these findings, we turn retrieval heads into a target of optimization by training their attention with a ranking objective. This raises the page Recall@1 of Qwen3-VL-8B on MMDocIR by 6.03 points and improves document retrieval across three model families. Functional attention heads can thus serve both as a lens on multimodal models and as a target for improving them.

papers.title: Singular Geometry of Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.abstract_en: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) is now a standard approach to parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large neural networks. Its low-rank factorization is inherently non-identifiable, making LoRA a singular statistical model whose learning complexity cannot be described by parameter dimension alone. We study this complexity using the real log canonical threshold (RLCT) from singular learning theory and how it depends on both the low-rank parameterization and the pretrained network. Under a local linearization, LoRA induces a low-rank trace regression model whose Kullback--Leibler geometry is controlled by a forward-backward covariance, constructed from activations and backpropagated sensitivities at the adapted layer. This covariance determines which low-rank perturbations are statistically observable. When it is nondegenerate along the relevant low-rank directions, we recover the classical learning complexity of reduced-rank regression; when its kernel meets these directions, additional statistically indistinguishable parameters change the singular geometry. We characterize this geometry locally through observable tangent directions and a residual singularity, and globally through affine linear sections of determinantal varieties. The global learning complexity need not be determined at a ground-truth parameter, as singularities on another rank stratum can dominate. We also introduce a curvature-corrected multi-temperature estimator of the RLCT. Experiments on multilayer perceptron and transformer architectures reveal strongly layer-dependent forward-backward geometry and show that ambient covariance degeneracy does not imply degeneracy along the low-rank directions relevant to adaptation.

papers.title: Supervised Source Separation of Electric Vehicle Interior Noise Using a Hybrid Transformer Architecture
papers.abstract_en: The interior sound of an electric vehicle is a superposition of several distinct noise contributions - wind noise, tire noise, powertrain (electric drive unit and inverter) noise, and auxiliary-drive noise - whose relative balance governs both the overall loudness and the perceived sound quality in the vehicle interior. Decomposing a recorded vehicle interior signal into these source contributions is a prerequisite for targeted acoustic engineering, but requires effortful measurement campaigns as well as expertise in the field of transfer path analysis. This work formulates the decomposition as a supervised, binaural source-separation problem with four target source contributions and adapts a hybrid time-spectrogram transformer architecture, originally developed for music demixing, to the domain of sound source separation for technical systems. To disambiguate source contributions, conditioning is introduced in the form of operating-state information, including electric drive speed, electric drive load, vehicle speed, and auxiliary-drive speed. Since isolated real-world reference stems are costly to obtain, the model is trained on a physics-based parametric data generator that synthesizes labeled component sounds from randomized virtual-vehicle hardware configurations and driving scenarios, so that the ground-truth contribution of each source is known by construction. Validation on both synthetic and measured vehicle interior sounds probes the achieved separation performance and underscores the feasibility of applying the proposed method for acoustic contribution analysis in technical systems.

papers.title: The Butterfly Defects: Tracing Cooperation in LLM Agent Networks
papers.abstract_en: As large language models (LLMs) increasingly operate as interconnected agents, a fundamental question emerges: does individual cooperation translate into collective cooperation? We investigate this question through the Iterated Prisoner's Dilemma (IPD), moving from dyadic interactions to homogeneous and heterogeneous networks of open-weight LLMs. Our findings reveal that cooperation is highly sensitive to model composition and seemingly minor linguistic changes. Models that cooperate with identical peers can shift toward defection in mixed populations. A simple uncertainty cue can increase or decrease cooperation, redistribute costs, and affect unexposed agents several hops away. Even reversing action-label order can dramatically alter behavior, with uncertainty framing sometimes amplifying this sensitivity. Together, these findings challenge the notion of cooperation as a stable model-level property, revealing how strategic behavior depends on interaction partners, network positions, and the language used to frame decisions.

papers.title: DealsFlow: An Evidence-Gated Agentic Harness for Venture Capital Deal Triage
papers.abstract_en: Large language models (LLMs) can read startup pitch decks, but letting them emit investment scores directly invites score inflation, run-to-run variance and rationales that are hard to audit. There, the full pipeline's score has Spearman $ρ=0.45$ (95% CI 0.32 to 0.57) with the total-value multiple and AUC 0.71 for identifying write-offs, against $ρ=0.38$ and AUC 0.68 for an unconstrained LLM. papers.title: VTRL-Med: Progressive Visual Refinement with Topology-Guided Regularization for Medical Image Clustering
papers.abstract_en: Deep clustering offers a promising approach for analyzing large unlabeled medical image datasets, yet prevailing methods still face two limitations: they may neglect class-agnostic structural priors that capture object boundaries and regions, and they do not explicitly encode topological patterns (e.g., connectivity and holes). We introduce VTRL-Med, a progressive visual-structural learning framework with topology-guided regularization for medical image clustering. It then generates reliable pseudo-labels through a two-step filtering process that combines prototype-based selection with k-nearest neighbor consistency validation. Finally, it progressively refines the visual branch while an auxiliary topology branch, constructed from persistent homology (PH) descriptors, provides additional geometric regularization during training. Across 13 medical image benchmarks, VTRL-Med achieves state-of-the-art clustering performance, improving average accuracy by 4.48% over existing methods. On three representative datasets, topology-guided regularization further improves accuracy by 1.3--4.3% over visual refinement alone.

papers.title: SemGeo-Gen: Unsupervised Generation of Approximate Cross-Instance Semantic-Geometric Correspondences
papers.abstract_en: We introduce SemGeo-Gen, an unsupervised method for generating approximate cross-instance semantic-geometric supervision from weakly aligned 3D object collections. papers.title: Trusting the Tool: Asymmetric Deference of LLM Vulnerability Auditors to Static-Analysis Evidence

papers.title: A Foundation Model for Policy In-Context Longitudinal Causal Effect Estimation
papers.abstract_en: Longitudinal causal effect estimation is complicated by time-varying confounding and treatment-confounder feedback loops. Given a new observational dataset and target policy, it directly predicts conditional average potential outcomes (CAPOs) in one forward pass without task-specific training or hyperparameter tuning. Across synthetic and semi-synthetic longitudinal benchmarks, PICLE-PFN achieves competitive RMSE and substantially improved uncertainty calibration with a fraction of deployment runtime, compared to state-of-the-art conventional estimators trained and tuned separately for each dataset.

papers.title: Probing the limits of forward screening and inverse design of crystal materials
papers.abstract_en: Crystal materials are designed either by screening known crystals for a target property or by generating new crystals with that property. Both routes are judged against public databases of known crystals, but these databases name the same crystal differently. Here we probe them by matching the crystals of 55 databases by structure into one self-extending database of 14.6 million crystals and 131.8 million property values, each traced to its source. Only 4.5% of its crystal-property pairs carry a value. To fill the empty pairs, we developed CGTNet, an equivariant graph transformer with state-of-the-art accuracy on several tasks of two public benchmarks. Trained on each task, it forms a library of property models whose predictions we release. The reach of forward screening has been underestimated. Known crystals hold tens of thousands of ultra-incompressible candidates without a recorded bulk modulus, and a post hoc audit of synthesis evidence finds among them ReN2, whose bulk modulus was measured at 428 GPa. The novelty claimed for inverse design has been overestimated. At an equal verification budget, a stiffness-conditioned generator returned more stiff hits than screening (100 versus 55), but all contained osmium and 82 repeated recorded compositions. Integrating and completing the databases of known crystals therefore moves the limits of both routes: it widens what screening can reach and sets the reference against which generated crystals are judged new.

papers.title: CoPiT: A conditional Position-induced Transformer for aerodynamic field prediction on unstructured meshes

On the AirfRANS full-data test set, CoPiT reduces surface and volume losses by approximately 54\% and 24\% relative to Transolver, respectively, and achieves the lowest overall normalized test MSE among the compared baselines on BlendedNet++. Matched ablations show that FiLM conditioning generally improves upon input concatenation, while the preferred placement is task-dependent. papers.title: SemantEq: Faithful Bidirectional Equivalence of Formal Statements
papers.abstract_en: Statement autoformalization translates mathematics from natural language into a proof assistant such as Lean 4, and models now do it at scale. As provers get stronger, the burden of correctness shifts from the proof to the statement, that is, to whether the formal statement faithfully translates its source. Given a trusted reference formalization, the natural test is logical equivalence, and it proves too much. $P \leftrightarrow Q$ holds trivially for any two statements $P$ and $Q$ that the library proves, because a prover can prove each separately and pass through $P \leftrightarrow \mathrm{True} \leftrightarrow Q$. The stronger the prover, the more unrelated pairs pass. Earlier methods restrict the prover and check that each proof names the other statement. We introduce SemantEq, a more principled relation that instead requires each statement to turn into the other only through a chain of allowed steps, such as logical rearrangement and rewriting with the library's own equations. Our programs judge a proof by the proof term Lean checks, not by its tactic script. SemantEq-Eval, a search without a model, reaches 100% precision and 65.6% recall on the ProofNetVerif test split under our adjudicated labels, against 95.8% and 61.8% for BEq+, and an 8.9-fold increase in its CPU time adds at most three pairs. A language model finds more proofs, but under two of four prompts it proves both directions of about two in five of the non-equivalent pairs. SemantEq-ProofAudit audits each model-written proof under a policy derived from the relation and accepts none of the 104 non-equivalent pairs, and it raises recall on 407 equivalent pairs from 65.4% to 81.1% under the best prompt. Separating the generation of equivalence proofs from their acceptance lets a stronger prover raise recall without changing what an acceptance means. papers.title: DRIVE: Fine-tuning via Data Contribution- and Diversity-aware Weighting with Prior Regularization

This is because current schemes privilege one goal over the other, and no explicit gradient-compatible encoding exists for such signals. To address this, we propose DRIVE, a principled and efficient weight assignment framework. It derives per-sample weights via a unified differentiable objective where three coupled signals co-evolve: Shapley additivity splits contribution into anti-forgetting and adaptation components, which are reshaped by a covariance-based diversity term and stabilized by a sample-characteristic prior. Far from a mere combination, this yields an end-to-end gradient-based scheme balancing stability against plasticity. Theoretically, we prove that DRIVE enjoys superior stability-plasticity guarantees over existing weighting schemes and enhances parameter estimation robustness. Empirically, it attains superior overall performance, faster convergence, and stronger robustness. Code at https://github.com/luciabcd/DRIVE.

papers.title: Where Rounding Happens Matters: Rounding-Location Alignment Stabilizes LLM Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning for large language models often uses separate systems for inference and training. We ask whether aligning selected parts of the execution stack can stabilize BF16 RL while other implementation differences remain. papers.title: LLaCO: Continuous Diffusion for Large Language Models with Competition-Aware Semantic Scheduling
papers.abstract_en: Continuous diffusion models have emerged as a promising non-autoregressive paradigm for text generation over continuous embedding spaces. Along the continuous trajectory, the residual token identity directly shapes the denoising objective. However, the geometric trajectory misaligns with temporal progression, triggering severe temporal compression. In this paper, we show that embedding norm decay causes Euclidean distance to yield spurious overtaking, indicating that token competition must be evaluated directionally. In this space, a candidate overtakes the source token only when the effective noise magnitude surpasses their semantic separation. We formalize these pairwise dynamics as the Competition Threshold Theory (CTT). Crucially, high-dimensional overtaking requires extreme noise levels, causing standard trajectories to concentrate identity decay into a narrow window near the noisy endpoint. To resolve this, we propose Semantic Retention Scheduling (SRS) to align time allocation with the progression of identity decay, and demonstrate that existing token identity metrics are fundamentally statistical aggregations of these pairwise crossings. Building on these theoretical insights, we introduce LLaCO, a generative framework powered by competition-aware semantic scheduling. LLaCO adapts a pretrained backbone to continuous representations via an embedding directional adapter and timestep-conditioned modulation. To operate within the directional space, LLaCO employs a spherical noising process formulated as a geodesic interpolation toward a mask-biased endpoint, eliminating norm decay while preserving accurate token competition. Guided by SRS, LLaCO reallocates the denoising trajectory proportionally to the logarithmic rank decay. Instantiated as an 8B model, LLaCO outperforms previous continuous diffusion baselines and rivals discrete diffusion models of comparable scale.
